extracted.intended_audience: news editors, reporters, photojournalists, digital journalists, newsroom leadership and entrants to ASNE awards
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation and eligibility criteria for the 2016 American Society of News Editors (ASNE) journalism awards, describing what each category honors and what judges looked for in entries. Useful for journalists and news organizations preparing submissions or understanding award standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for entry
rubrics_metrics.description: All news organizations, news services and online-only news sites in the United States, including those without an ASNE member on staff, were eligible to enter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contest drew more than 300 entries. Entries could be from organizations of a range of sizes and platforms. (Implicit guidance: entrants must be U.S.-based news organizations or services, including online-only sites.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: With the exception of the Batten Medal, which covered work published since 2013, the awards were given for work completed in 2015.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit work completed/published in the eligibility period specified for each award (2015 for most categories; Batten Medal covers a broader period since 2013).

rubrics_metrics.name: Batten Medal: public-service journalism values
rubrics_metrics.description: Honors public-service journalism in memory of James K. Batten; intended to celebrate the journalistic values Batten stood for: compassion, courage, humanity and a deep concern for the underdog.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges praise work that shows extraordinary effort and risk, compelling storytelling and profound humanity. Example judge comment: "Rubin showed readers... her courage, her compelling storytelling and her profound humanity would have made James Batten proud." Winning work example: Afghanistan reporting (Alissa Rubin).

rubrics_metrics.name: Burl Osborne Award for Editorial Leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes editorial writing that is excellent journalism and makes a difference in a community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges look for powerful, persuasive editorials that champion issues affecting communities, using solid research and searing sentiment to reach readers' minds and hearts. Example judge comment: "He uses solid research and searing sentiment to reach readers' minds and hearts." Winning work examples: editorials by Randy Essex.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deborah Howell Award for Nondeadline Writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes excellence in writing that's not accomplished on deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges value taut, sophisticated narrative, deep character development, nuanced reporting and writing that make the takeaway deeply felt. Example judge comment: "'An Unbelievable Story of Rape' is a taut, sophisticated narrative with deep character development and an astounding conclusion." Winning work example: 'An Unbelievable Story of Rape' (ProPublica/The Marshall Project).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dori J. Maynard Award for Diversity in Journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Celebrates journalism that overcomes ignorance, stereotypes, intolerance, racism or hate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges reward work that puts complex issues into human perspective, overcomes stereotypes, and uses storytelling devices (chaptering, podcasts) to provide a rare human look. Example judge comment: "The chaptering of the story brings the family into perspective... and with the accompanying podcasts, provides a rare human look at the issues." Winning work example: 'Divided by Law' (Arizona Daily Star).

rubrics_metrics.name: Frank A. Blethen Award for Local Accountability Reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes outstanding work done by a news organization that holds important local institutions accountable for their actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges favor investigative work that is deeply reported (e.g., extended embedding with families), rigorous data analysis ("analyzed millions of rows of records"), comparative context, and demonstrable impact (policy changes, investigations). Example judge comment: "The series resulted in immediate impact: creation of magnet programs... and even a federal investigation... exemplified the power and importance of local investigative reporting." Winning work example: 'Failure Factories' (Tampa Bay Times).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mike Royko Award for Commentary/Column Writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes excellence in writing by an individual that expresses a personal point of view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges look for deeply reported, gracefully written columns that capture complex emotions and use the columnist's voice to speak to and for the community with eloquence. Example judge comment: "He captures the grief and outrage... and he uses all power of his columnist voice to speak for and to the community with great eloquence." Winning work examples: multiple columns by David Cook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punch Sulzberger Award for Online Storytelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes excellence and innovation in the use of digital tools to tell news stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges favor digital storytelling that is seamless and immersive, with multimedia elements employed with purpose and precision to enhance and drive the story (use of video, audio, 3-D modeling). Example judge comment: "This entry stood out for its clarity... multimedia elements with purpose and precision... uses 3-D modeling and video to take readers on an immersive tour." Winning work examples: Michael Kimmelman's architecture reviews ('Dear Architects: Sound Matters', 'A New Whitney').

rubrics_metrics.name: Breaking News Writing Award
rubrics_metrics.description: Awarded for accurate, trustworthy, comprehensive and up-to-the-minute coverage of breaking events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges value clear, crisp writing and sharp editing that deliver key information without clutter, comprehensive coverage by a dispersed staff, and reporting informed by deep institutional knowledge of the community and its tensions. Example judge comment: "The writing was clear and crisp, and the editing was sharp... reporting was informed by The Sun staff's deep institutional knowledge." Winning work example: coverage of the death of Freddie Gray and ensuing riots (The Baltimore Sun).

rubrics_metrics.name: Community Service Photojournalism Award
rubrics_metrics.description: Rewards photography that captures the sense of a community with powerful and meaningful images and provides an understanding of the community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges look for photos that go beyond predictable scenes to capture moments revealing passion, complexity and meaning about the community. Example judge comment: "They didn't find just scenes, they captured moments... the passion and complexity of that week in Baltimore were revealed." Winning work example: Photos of the Freddie Gray unrest (The Baltimore Sun).
